subject.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup

question: Should `sessions cleanup --enforce` be allowed to physically remove stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files according to the existing retention rules and report that in dry-run/apply output?
rationale: The patch is a narrow owner-boundary fix, but accepting removal of retained session archive artifacts is a product/session-state decision that automation should not make for maintainers.

options.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
options.body: Land the PR as-is if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention rules and current CLI proof.

options.title: Ask for broader upgrade proof
options.body: Pause for a larger real-store or upgrade-style cleanup transcript if maintainers want more confidence before changing retained-artifact behavior.

options.title: Defer to retention policy work
options.body: Hold or close the PR if maintainers want to settle the broader no-delete/archive naming policy before changing cleanup behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the PR as-is if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention rules and current CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sessions cleanup UX and maintenance controls that this PR changes at the operator boundary.
